title: The Declaration of Independence
subtitle: Thirteen colonies, one hot summer in Philadelphia, and a letter to a king.
description: An A2 reading and listening text on the Declaration of Independence: why the colonies were angry, who wrote the document, and what happened on 4 July 1776.
source: authored for this site; no source document
passage: In the summer of 1776, a small group of men sat in a hot room in Philadelphia and decided to leave their country.
At that time, thirteen colonies on the Atlantic coast belonged to Britain. The king was George III, and he lived more than five thousand kilometres away.

The colonists were angry about taxes. Britain made them pay money for tea, paper and other things, but the colonists had nobody in the British parliament. They said: no taxation without representation.
The war with Britain started in 1775. For more than a year the colonies fought, but they still called themselves British.
Then, in June 1776, a group called the Continental Congress asked five men to write a document. The document had to explain to the world why America wanted to be a separate country.
One of the five men did most of the writing. His name was Thomas Jefferson, and he was thirty-three years old. He worked on it for about two weeks.
The most famous sentence is short: “all men are created equal”. Jefferson wrote that people have rights that no king can take away: life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness.
Congress discussed the text and changed parts of it. On 4 July 1776, they accepted it. Most of the men signed it one month later, in August.
There is a hard fact behind the beautiful words. Jefferson wrote that all men are equal, and Jefferson owned enslaved people. So did many of the other men in the room.
Americans celebrate the fourth of July every year with family dinners, music and fireworks. The war, however, continued for seven more years.

vocabulary.definition: an area controlled by another country (people there are colonists)
money that people must pay to a government
the group of people who make the laws in Britain
having somebody who speaks for you in a government
to write your name on a document
the things everybody should be allowed to have or do
the same as somebody else in value or importance
to do something special because of an important day

items.explanation: Thirteen colonies on the Atlantic coast. The thirteen stripes on the flag are those colonies.

items.prompt: Why were the colonists angry about taxes?
options: They had nobody in the British parliament
items.explanation: “No taxation without representation”: they paid, but nobody spoke for them in parliament.

items.prompt: Who did most of the writing?
items.explanation: Five men were asked, but Jefferson did most of the writing.

items.prompt: When did Congress accept the Declaration?
items.explanation: They accepted it on 4 July 1776. Most of them signed it in August.

items.prompt: What does the text say about Jefferson and slavery?
options: He never met an enslaved person
items.explanation: He wrote that all men are equal, and he owned enslaved people. The text asks you to hold both facts at the same time.

options: The war continued for seven more years
items.explanation: Declaring independence and winning it are two different things. The war went on until 1783.

exercises.title: True or False?
exercises.instructions: Decide if each sentence is true or false.

items.statement: The war started after the Declaration.
items.explanation: False — the war started in 1775, more than a year before the Declaration.

items.statement: Jefferson was over sixty when he wrote it.
items.explanation: False — he was thirty-three.

items.statement: Congress changed parts of Jefferson's text.
items.explanation: True — “Congress discussed the text and changed parts of it.”

items.statement: King George III lived in America.
items.explanation: False — he lived more than five thousand kilometres away, in Britain.

items.statement: Americans celebrate the fourth of July every year.
items.explanation: True — with family dinners, music and fireworks.

exercises.title: Vocabulary in Use
exercises.instructions: Choose the best word for each sentence.

items.prompt: Money that people must pay to a government is a ___.
items.explanation: A tax. The verb is also tax: Britain taxed tea and paper.

items.prompt: To write your name on a document is to ___ it.
items.explanation: To sign. The men signed the Declaration in August 1776.
Liberty. It is in the famous sentence: life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness.

items.prompt: If two people have the same value and importance, they are ___.
items.explanation: Equal. “All men are created equal.”

items.prompt: Having somebody who speaks for you in a government is ___.
items.explanation: Representation — the key word in the colonists' slogan.

exercises.title: Complete the Summary
exercises.instructions: Complete the summary with one word in each gap.

items.prompt: Thirteen ___ on the Atlantic coast belonged to Britain.
items.explanation: Colonies. A colony is controlled by another country.

items.prompt: The colonists said: no taxation without ___.
items.explanation: Representation.

items.prompt: Thomas ___ did most of the writing.
items.explanation: Jefferson. Washington was leading the army at the time; Lincoln was born in 1809.

items.prompt: Congress accepted the document on ___ July 1776.
items.explanation: The fourth of July.

items.prompt: Americans ___ this day every year with fireworks.
items.explanation: Celebrate.

discussion: Does your country have a national day? What happened on that date?
The Declaration says people have a right to “life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness”. What rights do you think are most important?
Jefferson wrote that all men are equal, and he owned enslaved people. How should a country remember a person like that?
